newsitem.title: USA: PS Enterprise sees Salem 2 return boost.
newsitem.headline: PS Enterprise sees Salem 2 return boost.

text.p: Public Service Enterprise Group Inc said Tuesday its operations will receive a boost in the next few weeks when the Salem 2 nuclear unit returns to service.

The company reported second quarter earnings of $91.5 million, or $0.39 per share, down from $134.5 million, or $0.55 per share, a year earlier, when there was a gain of $0.07 a share from the repurchase of Public Service Electric and Gas Co cumulative preferred stock.
The First Call consensus estimate for the latest quarter was $0.47 per share.
This year, the company said, electric sales by PSE&G were lower due to considerably cooler weather during the 1997 period, which affected air conditioning use, particularly by residential customers.

This had a net negative impact on overall electric and gas sales of about $0.03 per share. Higher administrative costs in the quarter, about $0.04 per share, were primarily attributable to issues related to the Salem outage.
Startup costs, amounting to about $0.02 per share, were incurred by Energis Resources, Enterprise's energy management company established in January of this year.

"Enterprise's operations are fundamentally strong across the board and will receive a noteworthy boost in the next few weeks with the return to service of our Salem 2 nuclear unit," said chief executive E. James Ferland.
"On a continuing basis, we look forward to solid contributions from both our utility and non-utility businesses."
Second quarter 1997 earnings for PSE&G were $81.2 million, or $0.35 per share, of Enterprise common stock, compared with $119.8 million, or $0.49 per share, a year earlier.

Earnings for Enterprise Diversified Holdings Inc, parent company of Enterprise's non-regulated businesses, were $10.3 million, or $0.04 per share of Enterprise common stock, compared with $14.7 million, or $0.06 per share, last year.

The company said PSE&G's electric sales through June decreased 4.2 percent from 1996's first half level. Residential, commercial and industrial sales were down 4.8 percent, 4.2 percent and 3.4 percent, respectively.
Electric sales in the second quarter declined 3.7 percent from a year earlier, with residential, commercial and industrial sales down by 4.0 percent, 3.8 percent and 3.3 percent, respectively.
